definitions.explanation: The technique of briefly searing the surface of food (especially sushi and sashimi) with an open flame, or food prepared this way. The searing adds a smoky flavor while keeping the inside raw.

examples.japanese: {炙|あぶ}りサーモンが{人気|にんき}だ。
バーナーでの{炙|あぶ}りが{料理|りょうり}の{味|あじ}を{引|ひ}き{立|た}てる。
examples.english: Torching enhances the flavor of the dish.

examples.japanese: この{店|みせ}の{炙|あぶ}り{寿司|ずし}は{注文|ちゅうもん}を{受|う}けてから{目|め}の{前|まえ}で{炙|あぶ}ってくれる。
examples.english: At this restaurant, the seared sushi is torched right in front of you after you order.

notes:
USAGE:
{炙|あぶ}り is used both as a noun (the technique or the dish) and as a prefix before the ingredient name. It has become popular at conveyor-belt sushi restaurants and modern sushi bars.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {炙|あぶ}りサーモン (seared salmon)
- {炙|あぶ}り{寿司|ずし} (seared sushi)
- {炙|あぶ}り{鯖|さば} (seared mackerel)
- {炙|あぶ}りトロ (seared fatty tuna)

From the verb {炙|あぶ}る (to broil, to sear over an open flame).
